chapter: Part Two: theaters and the Chicago scene
title: The Metropolitan Theater and Erskine Tate's 1929 band
summary: Personnel and arranging for Tate's orchestra at the Met.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Where was the Metropolitan Theater?
47th and Parkway, which is King Drive, now.
And whose band were you in then?
Erskine Tate.
Erskine Tate. And were you still playing for silent movies then, or were you playing for the show?
Yeah, we were playing silent movies.
When was this?
Must have been '29.
Talkies were just about to come in?
Just about to come in.
Was that the band that Tate had that Louie was in? No, Louie was gone by then.
Yeah, Louie was gone by then.
Yeah. Who was in that Tate band, do you remember?
Well, there was his brother on trumpet, James Tate. Bob S Hoffner on trumpet, and first part was John Thomas on trombone. Then later on we got Louis Taylor
on trombone.
Is that when you first met Louis Taylor?
No, I knew him from high school days.
Oh, he's another --
He's another --
Wendell Phillips?
Yeah. Him and Wallace Bishop, the drummer.
He went to --

He went to Phillips, yeah. And Jerome Carrington on piano. And Omer Simeon on clarinet and saxophone. And -- heck, what was the third sax man? Charlie Harris on sax. And what was Thomas' name on oboe? He was from the West Indies.
Played oboe?
Played oboe.
Didn't double, just played oboe?
Didn't double, just played oboe.
Who made the arrangements for that band?
Omer Simeon and myself.
Were you doing a lot of arranging at this time?
As I said before, just special
saxophone courses, special brass courses.
